title: Observability Infrastructure
description: Health of the observability pipeline itself — Prometheus scrape targets and the OpenTelemetry Collector's own internal metrics (job="otel-collector", scraped from its :8888 self-telemetry endpoint) — not the four application services' business metrics (see the Application Health dashboard for those). Every metric on this dashboard was queried against a real running stack before being added here; none are assumed from documentation.

panels.title: Scrape Target Availability
panels.description: up{job="prometheus"|"otel-collector"|"otel-collector-app-metrics"} — 1 means Prometheus successfully scraped that target on its most recent attempt, 0 means the scrape failed. These are the only three scrape jobs configured in observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml.

panels.title: Collector Telemetry Ingestion (Accepted vs. Refused)
panels.description: otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans, otelcol_receiver_accepted_metric_points, otelcol_receiver_refused_spans, and otelcol_receiver_refused_metric_points, by receiver — confirms the Collector's OTLP receiver is actually accepting telemetry from the four application services, and surfaces any refused spans or refused metric points specifically (both are separately queried below, not just spans). Refused counts should be 0 under normal operation; a sustained nonzero refused rate for either would indicate a real ingestion problem (e.g. malformed payloads).

panels.title: Collector Export Health (Sent Spans + Queue Size)
panels.description: otelcol_exporter_sent_spans by exporter ("debug" and "otlp_grpc/tempo" — the traces pipeline's two exporters) and otelcol_exporter_queue_size by exporter/data_type. A persistently nonzero or growing queue size relative to otelcol_exporter_queue_capacity would indicate the Collector cannot export as fast as it receives (backpressure toward Tempo or the debug log).

panels.title: Collector Process Health
panels.description: otelcol_process_uptime (seconds since the Collector process last started — a reset to near-zero means it restarted) and otelcol_process_memory_rss, confirming the Collector container itself is a single continuously-running process, not silently crash-looping.
